title: Proof-of-concept for Use of Transcutaneous Spinal Stimulation (TSS) With the ExaStim® Stimulation System in Adults With Chronic Ischemic Stroke
official: Proof-of-concept for Use of Transcutaneous Spinal Stimulation (TSS) With the ExaStim® Stimulation System in Chronic Stroke Population
summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn about the safety, tolerability, and feasibility of ExaStim transcutaneous electrical stimulation combined with task-specific rehabilitation, and to characterize changes in arm function in adults with chronic unilateral ischemic stroke. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does 12 weeks of ExaStim stimulation combined with structured, task-specific rehabilitation improve arm function?
* What are the safety, tolerability, and feasibility of ExaStim use in individuals with chronic stroke?

Participants will:

* Complete a 12-week intervention period combining ExaStim transcutaneous electrical stimulation with structured, task-specific rehabilitation
* Undergo clinical assessments and outcome testing baseline, week 4, week 8, week 12, and week 17 (follow-up)
* Monitor and report pain and quality of life via Visual Analog Scales (VAS) and questionnaires throughout the 17-week study duration
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

1. Subject must have a documented diagnosis of a singular unilateral ischemic stroke event confirmed by radiology report.
2. Participant is in the chronic stage of neurological recovery, defined as at least 6 months after the unilateral ischemic stroke event.
3. Subject is aged 18-75 years
4. In the investigators or qualified clinician's judgment, the subject must possess sufficient global cognitive capacity to understand and follow study-related instructions, actively participate in task-specific rehabilitation, and provide informed consent. Cognitive capacity will be supported by the subject's ability to follow a three-step command and demonstrate orientation to person, place, time, and situation (4/4)
5. Subject must have a Fugl-Meyer Assessment-Upper Extremity (FMA-UE) score between 20 and 50 (inclusive) at screening.
6. Subject must be able to commit to participating in a 17-week study, and be willing to comply with study instructions, agree to make all office and therapy appointments, and complete the entire course of the study
7. Subject must be deemed medically stable for intensive physical rehabilitation and transcutaneous electrical stimulation, supported by formal written clearance from their primary care physician or managing neurologist.
8. Subject must be able to understand the study, provide informed consent, and complete the applicable HIPAA authorization using IRB-approved procedures. Literacy alone is not an exclusion. IRB-approved accessible consent methods may be used when needed, while the investigator confirms the participant's own understanding, decision-making capacity, and ability to meet study communication requirements.

Exclusion Criteria:

1. Active implanted medical device for electrical stimulation
2. Index stroke is hemorrhagic or involves the brainstem, cerebellum, or thalamus, as confirmed by neuroimaging or medical records.
3. Other internal metallic objects of unknown or foreign origin (unidentifiable surgical implants, shrapnel, bullet fragments, etc.)
4. Botox injections to the upper limb(s) in prior 3 months
5. Severe spasticity, MAS grade \>3 (grade 4 only; grade 3 is not excluded by this criterion) in any of the following muscles: shoulder abductors, shoulder flexors, elbow flexors/extensors, wrist flexion, forearm supination or pronation, or finger flexors.
6. Subject scores \<20 or \>50 points on the FMA-UE.
7. BMI \> 40.0 (morbid obesity)
8. Acute medical conditions under active treatment that would contraindicate standard rehabilitation including open wounds, unhealed bone fractures, peripheral neuropathies or painful musculoskeletal dysfunction
9. Subjects who are pregnant or planned pregnancy during the study. Participants of childbearing potential must agree to effective contraception for the duration of participation.
10. Allergy to hydrogel, silicone, latex or other product materials
11. Compromised skin in the area for electrode contact (back of neck and/or hip area)
12. Uncontrolled cardiopulmonary disease or hypertension
13. Presence of ongoing dysphagia or aspiration difficulties.
14. Significant sensory impairments. Subjects who score below a 6 out of 12 on the sensory subscale (section H) of the Fugl Meyer Assessment will be excluded.
15. Other symptoms that would prohibit use or cause discomfort from stimulation such as hypersensitivity.
16. History of more than one stroke episode
17. Severe contractures of upper extremity(s)
18. Severe receptive and/or expressive aphasia limiting communication and understanding of device and interventions
19. History of uncontrolled epilepsy or seizures
20. Unmanaged depression, psychiatric disorders or ongoing substance abuse
21. Participation in another clinical trial that may interfere with this study
